title: The Battle of the Monkey and the Crab
text:
A crab found a rice ball, and a monkey found a persimmon seed. The monkey talked the crab into trading, pointing out that a seed would grow into a tree that would give fruit for years. The crab planted the seed and cared for it, and in time it became a tree covered with persimmons.

The crab could not climb, so the monkey offered to pick the fruit. Up in the tree, he ate the ripe ones himself and threw a hard green persimmon down at the crab, wounding her so badly that she died. In some versions she is only injured.

The crab's children wanted justice, but they were small, and the monkey was big and strong. So they asked for help, and a chestnut, a bee, a heavy rice mortar and a lump of cow dung joined them. While the monkey was out, they slipped into his house and each took a position.

When the monkey came home and sat by the hearth to warm himself, the chestnut burst out of the fire and burned him. He ran for water, and the bee stung him. He fled, slipped on the cow dung by the door, and fell, and the mortar dropped from the roof onto him. The crabs had their revenge.
lesson: Small allies who each contribute one exact ability, placed at the right moment, can bring down someone much stronger. Plan the whole sequence, not only your own part.
people: The crab and her children, a chestnut, a bee, a mortar, cow dung, the monkey
date: Japanese folk tradition, recorded from the Edo period
caveat: The allies and the exact sequence differ between versions.
